simple.meaning: יָעָה (yâʻâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to brush aside.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Isaiah, beginning at Isaiah 28:17. The surrounding contexts include righteousness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָעָה (H3261) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: יָעָה (yâʻâh) / H3261 is traced through Isaiah 28:17 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H3261. yaah יָעָה verb sweep together (with collateral idea of carrying away ) (Arabic is collect, gather ) — Qal Perfect וְיָעָה consecutive Isa 28:17 subject בָּרָד with accusative ( ב ׳ויעה כָזָב מַחְסֵה ). **Compare also Arabic vessel Gen 42:25 Saad, compare Baldensperger PEF 1904, 53, who compares Modern Arabic wa±â ().

occurrences.englishText: I will make justice the measuring line, and righteousness the plumb line. The hail will sweep away the refuge of lies, and the waters will overflow the hiding place.
